name: Antonín Dvořák
basis: Based in Prague: organist at St Vojtěch until 1876 and Prague premieres 1877-1881 (Wikipedia)

name: Arcangelo Corelli
basis: Op.1-4 published in Rome 1681-1694 and he spent most of his career there; only a brief Modena stay 1689-90 (Wikipedia)

name: Béla Bartók
basis: Piano professor at the Liszt Academy in Budapest from 1907; 1908 folk-collecting trips from Budapest (Wikipedia)

name: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach
basis: In Frederick the Great's service in Berlin 1738-1768, then Kapellmeister in Hamburg 1768-1788 (Wikipedia)

name: Clara Schumann
timeline: start: Leipzig; from 1845: Dresden; from 1850: Düsseldorf
basis: Leipzig after 1840 marriage, Schumanns moved to Dresden 1844 and Düsseldorf 1850; Brahms visited them in Düsseldorf in 1853 (Wikipedia; move years from Robert Schumann timeline)

name: Claude Debussy
basis: Bought a house off the Avenue du Bois de Boulogne in Paris in 1905, his home for the rest of his life (Wikipedia)

name: Claudio Monteverdi
timeline: start: Cremona; from 1591: Mantua; from 1613: Venice
basis: Entered Gonzaga service in Mantua 1590/91, maestro at St Mark's Venice from Aug 1613, died Venice 1643 so 1650-51 posthumous prints are Venetian (Wikipedia)

name: Domenico Scarlatti
basis: Followed Maria Barbara to Madrid in 1733 and remained at the Spanish court until his death there in 1757 (Wikipedia)

name: Edvard Grieg
basis: Settled in Christiania 1866, gave up fixed work there 1874, then 1874-85 no single base (tours, Hardanger/Lofthus, Bergen); Troldhaugen near Bergen home from April 1885 - so 1878 and 1883 are only approximately Bergen (SNL; Troldhaugen Wikipedia)

name: Erwin Schulhoff
basis: Returned to Prague 1923, joined the Prague Conservatory faculty 1929 and worked there in the early 1930s (Wikipedia)

name: Felix Mendelssohn
timeline: start: Berlin; from 1833: Düsseldorf; from 1835: Leipzig
basis: Berlin-based 1827-29, musical director in Düsseldorf 1833, Gewandhaus director in Leipzig from 1835 and died there Nov 1847 (Encyclopedia.com)

name: Francis Poulenc
basis: Lived with his sister on Rue de Monceau, Paris from 1917; mobilised Jan 1918 at Vincennes then posted to the War Ministry in Paris until 1921 (poulenc.fr)

name: Franz Liszt
basis: Kapellmeister at Weimar from 1848 until he left in 1861 (Deutsche Grammophon biography)

name: Franz Schubert
basis: Vienna-based throughout; 'from 1826 to 1828 Schubert resided continuously in Vienna' apart from a brief Graz visit 1827 (New World Encyclopedia)

name: François Couperin
basis: Organist at Saint-Gervais Paris and from 1717 ordinaire de la musique de la chambre du roi; Paris residence (Wikipedia)

name: Frédéric Chopin
basis: Lived in Warsaw until 2 Nov 1830, Vienna interim, arrived Paris 5 Oct 1831 and lived there until death 1849 (New World Encyclopedia)

name: Georg Friedrich Händel
basis: Settled permanently in London 1712; director of the Royal Academy of Music 1720-1728 (New World Encyclopedia)
source_title: George Frideric Handel - New World Encyclopedia

name: Giovanni Battista Pergolesi
basis: Active in Naples (Il Flaminio 1735, Stabat Mater premiered Naples 1736); died March 1736 at nearby Pozzuoli (Wikipedia)

name: Girolamo Frescobaldi
timeline: start: Rome; from 1628: Florence; from 1634: Rome
basis: Leave from St Peter's Nov 1628 for Florence, returned to Rome April 1634 to serve the Barberini; Fiori musicali published 1635 (Wikipedia)

name: Gustav Mahler
basis: Director of the Vienna Hofoper 1897-1907; summers composing at Maiernigg (Wikipedia)

name: Heinrich Schütz
basis: Dresden court Kapellmeister from 1615; returned from Copenhagen 1635 and next Danish visit only 1641, so 1636-39 in Dresden (Wikipedia)

name: Ignaz Pleyel
basis: Moved to Strasbourg 1783 as assistant maître de chapelle at the cathedral; Strasbourg period 1783-1793 (Wikipedia)

name: Jacopo Peri
basis: Florentine church musician and Medici court composer; Euridice first performed 6 Oct 1600 (New World Encyclopedia)

name: Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck
basis: Organist of the Oude Kerk Amsterdam from c.1580 for the rest of his life; died Amsterdam 16 Oct 1621 (Wikipedia)

name: Johann Christian Bach
basis: Composer to the King's Theatre London from 1762; remained in London until death 1 Jan 1782 (Wikipedia)

name: Johann Sebastian Bach
timeline: start: Weimar; from 1717: Köthen; from 1723: Leipzig
basis: Weimar 1708-1717, Köthen court 1717-1723 (1720, 1722 pieces), Thomaskantor in Leipzig 1723-1750 (1723, 1725, 1742, 1749 pieces) (EBSCO)
source_title: Johann Sebastian Bach - EBSCO Research Starters

name: Leopold Koželuch
basis: Moved to Vienna 1778 and was based there for the rest of his career; founded his publishing firm there 1784 (Wikipedia)

name: Ludwig van Beethoven
basis: Left Bonn for Vienna in November 1792 and never returned; died Vienna 1827 (Austria-Forum)
source_title: Biography of Ludwig van Beethoven - Austria-Forum

name: Maurice Ravel
basis: Paris Conservatoire student (readmitted to Fauré's class 1901; Prix de Rome affair 1905) and Paris resident (Wikipedia)

name: Nikolai Medtner
timeline: start: Moscow; from 1921: Berlin; from 1924: Paris
basis: Lived in Moscow until he left Russia in 1921 for Berlin, moved to France in 1924 (while touring North America 1924-25), settled in London Oct 1935 (medtner.org.uk)

name: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
basis: Professor at the Moscow Conservatory 1866-1878, combining teaching with criticism 1867-78 (Wikipedia)

name: Richard Wagner
basis: Completed Tristan in Lucerne in 1859 (Venice stay was 1858) and lived at Tribschen, Lucerne 1865/66-1872 (Wagnerstätten)
source_title: Stages of Richard Wagner's Life - Wagnerstätten

name: Robert Schumann
timeline: start: Leipzig; from 1845: Dresden; from 1850: Düsseldorf
basis: Leipzig-based (NZfM 1834; six-month Vienna stay 1838-39 only), moved to Dresden 1844, municipal music director in Düsseldorf from 1850 (World History Encyclopedia timeline)
source_title: Robert Schumann Timeline - World History Encyclopedia

name: Sergei Rachmaninoff
basis: Settled in New York 1918, Riverside Drive apartment from 1921 as home base; summers 1929-31 at Clairefontaine France, Senar not yet built (Wikipedia)

name: Wilhelm Friedemann Bach
timeline: start: Dresden; from 1746: Halle; from 1774: Berlin
basis: Organist in Dresden 1733-1746, Halle Liebfrauenkirche 1746-1764, Braunschweig 1771-74, Berlin from 1774 until death there 1784 (Wikipedia)

name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
timeline: start: Salzburg; from 1766: The Hague; from 1767: Salzburg; from 1778: Paris; from 1779: Salzburg; from 1781: Vienna
basis: In The Hague Sept 1765-Mar 1766 (K.24, K.26-31 written there), home in Salzburg Nov 1766; Konzertmeister Salzburg from 1772; Paris 1778; Vienna from March 1781 (Mozart family grand tour Wikipedia; World History Encyclopedia)

name: Augusta Mary Anne Holmès
basis: Born in Paris, raised in Versailles, central figure of Parisian musical and literary salons; died Versailles 1903 - Paris is the nearest gazetteer city (Wikipedia)

name: Claude Goudimel
basis: Moved to Metz 1557; dedicated psalters there 1564 and 1565 and stood godfather in Metz on 18 March 1565 (Wikipedia)

name: Cécile Chaminade
basis: Paris-born and Paris-trained, living near Paris (Le Vésinet) in 1901; source gives no residence for 1890 specifically, so Paris kept (Wikipedia)

name: Emilie Mayer
basis: Moved to Berlin in 1847 to study with A. B. Marx; concert of her works there 21 April 1850 (Wikipedia)

name: Emilie Zumsteeg
basis: Born in Stuttgart and lived there her whole life; died Stuttgart 1857 (Wikipedia)

name: Ernest Chausson
basis: Paris Conservatoire 1879-80 then private pupil of Franck in Paris until 1883; 1882 Bayreuth trip only a visit (Bru Zane Mediabase)

name: Fanny Hensel
basis: Berlin family home and Sonntagskonzerte throughout 1838-46 (Italy trip 1839-40 only); died Berlin 1847 (Wikipedia)

name: Franz Joseph Haydn
timeline: start: Eszterháza; from 1791: London; from 1793: Vienna; from 1795: London; from 1796: Vienna
basis: Esterházy Kapellmeister at Eisenstadt/Eszterháza 1761-90 (1772 Farewell Symphony), London Jan 1791-1792, Vienna 1792-94 (bought Gumpendorf house 1793), London 1794-mid Aug 1795, then Vienna (Austria-Forum)

name: Harry Thacker Burleigh
basis: Soloist at St George's Episcopal Church New York 1894-1946 and Temple Emanu-El choir 1900-1925 (Wikipedia)

name: Henry Purcell
basis: Organist of Westminster Abbey from 1679; family lived a few hundred yards west of the Abbey (Wikipedia)

name: Hugo Wolf
basis: Vienna-based; composed the Mörike-Lieder in 1888 at Perchtoldsdorf just outside Vienna (Wikipedia)

name: Johanna Kinkel
basis: Berlin 1836-c.1839, then back in Bonn: Singspiel Das Malzthier performed Bonn 18 March 1840, Maikäferbund in Bonn 1840-41; emigrated to London only 1851 (MUGI)

name: Johannes Brahms
basis: Hamburg-based through the 1850s (concerto premiere there Jan 1859; Detmold winters), Wiener Singakademie conductor 1863 and made Vienna his home; Gesellschaft concerts 1872-75 (Wikipedia)

name: Josephine Lang
basis: Lived in Munich until her 1842 marriage to C. R. Köstlin and move to Tübingen; died Tübingen 1880 (Stadt Tübingen Komponistinnen)

name: Louise Reichardt
basis: Moved to Hamburg in 1809 and composed there 1809-1826 (Wikipedia)

name: Maria Theresia von Paradis
basis: European tour 1783-86 (Paris 1784, London 1784-85, Hamburg, Berlin, Prague) ended with her return to Vienna in 1786 (Wikipedia)

name: Marie Jaëll
basis: Resided in Paris for most of her life, but in 1880 she and Alfred Jaëll were touring Europe and Russia; no source pins the 1880 base, Paris kept (KVAST; Wikipedia)

name: Mathilde Kralik
basis: Family moved to Vienna 1870, Vienna Conservatory 1876-78, works performed at the Musikverein 1894-95; lived in Vienna thereafter (Wikipedia)

name: Maude Valérie White
basis: Returned to London in 1882 after Chile and built her career there; 1883 Vienna study trip lasted only six months (Wikipedia)

name: Mel Bonis
basis: Parisian by birth and Paris Conservatoire training; resumed composing 1894 while living as Mme Domange in Paris, buried Montmartre (Wikipedia; source does not name 1895 address)

name: Pauline Viardot
basis: Returned to France after 1870, taught at the Paris Conservatoire and presided over a salon on the Boulevard Saint-Germain until 1883 (Wikipedia)

name: Robert Franz
basis: City organist, Singakademie conductor and university music director in his native Halle until 1868 (Wikipedia)

name: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor
basis: Lived in Croydon (now Greater London) from childhood until death 1912; 1904 US tour was a visit (Wikipedia)

name: Art Pepper
basis: Lived for many years in Echo Park, Los Angeles; photo captioned 'Pepper in Los Angeles, 1979' (Wikipedia).

name: Ben Webster
timeline: start: New York; from 1952: Los Angeles; from 1957: New York; from 1965: Copenhagen
basis: Foundation biography says that from 1952 he 'spent his time between Los Angeles and New York' with no relocation dates; Wikipedia adds late-1950s regular work at the LA club Renaissance and difficulty finding New York work in the early 1960s, so no single base is fixed for 1956/1959/1962 - ours kept.
source_title: Ben Webster Biography - Ben Webster Foundation

name: Benny Carter
timeline: start: New York; from 1943: Los Angeles
basis: Settled permanently in Los Angeles in 1945 (film and TV composing) and died there in 2003, so Los Angeles holds for both 1952 and 1986 (Britannica).

name: Benny Goodman
basis: Band resident at Chicago's Congress Hotel until May 1936, then Hollywood for the summer of 1936 (Camel Caravan from 30 June 1936), after which the band was New York-based (Carnegie Hall planned late 1937) (Wikipedia).

name: Bix Beiderbecke
basis: 1927 Trumbauer sessions (Feb, May) made in New York; Goldkette band folded in New York Sept 1927; joined Whiteman Oct 1927, whose 1928 sessions were mostly in New York (Wikipedia) - so both piece years map to New York as in our timeline.

name: Bob Berg
basis: Brooklyn-born, 'often played at the 7th Avenue South NYC club', died in East Hampton NY; no other base documented for 1979-97 (Wikipedia).

name: Branford Marsalis
basis: Wikipedia gives no base for 1988: Berklee (Boston) as a student, Blakey and Wynton's bands to 1985, School Daze 1988, later Michigan State 1996-2000; New York kept as default.

name: Buck Clayton
basis: Count Basie orchestra 'based in New York City' from 1937 with Clayton freelancing in NY studios; with Basie until drafted Nov 1943, army service to 1946 (Wikipedia).

name: Cannonball Adderley
basis: Moved to New York City in 1955; known address in Corona, Queens; Miles Davis Quintet from Oct 1957 (Wikipedia).

name: Charlie Parker
timeline: start: New York; from 1946: Los Angeles; from 1947: New York
basis: Town Hall concert New York June 1945; went to Los Angeles Dec 1945 and stayed in California (Camarillo State Hospital six months) until early 1947; 'upon returning to New York in 1947'; living in NYC from 1950 (Wikipedia).

name: Charlie Shavers
basis: New York-born; trumpet soloist and arranger of John Kirby's Sextet 1936-45 (Wikipedia).

name: Chet Baker
timeline: start: Los Angeles; from 1960: Paris; from 1975: New York
basis: Quartet a regular at Los Angeles clubs (The Haig, Tiffany Club) 1953-55, back to Los Angeles after the Sept 1955 European tour; in 1975 toured Europe and lived with Ruth Young 'while stopping in New York' (Wikipedia).

name: Chris Potter
basis: Studied at The New School and Manhattan School of Music, worked with Red Rodney in New York 1992-93, and is 'currently based in New York City' (Wikipedia).

name: Chu Berry
basis: Member of Cab Calloway's orchestra 1937-41 and a regular at Minton's Playhouse jam sessions in New York City; no other base documented (Wikipedia).

name: Clifford Brown
timeline: start: Los Angeles; from 1955: New York
basis: In the Los Angeles area March-Aug 1954, where the Brown-Roach quintet formed and he married; then 'returned to the East Coast' (Dec 1954 Sarah Vaughan session) and toured from there 1955-56 (Wikipedia) - New York used as the East Coast recording base.

name: Coleman Hawkins
basis: Returned from Europe in 1939 and recorded Body and Soul in New York (Oct 1939, Kelly's Stables); c.1945-50 'divided his time between New York and Europe'; 1954 Savoy/Jazztone albums (Wikipedia).

name: Curtis Fuller
basis: Lateef quintet 'moved to New York in 1957' where Fuller made his first Prestige sessions; joined Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers 1961 (Wikipedia).

name: David Liebman
basis: Milkowski: Liebman moved to New York City in 1980 and gigged there with Quest through the 1980s; he later lived in Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania (jazz.com has him in the Poconos by 2001) but no source gives the move date, so 1992/1996 are unsettled - New York kept.
source_title: Thinking of the Great Dave Liebman - Bill Milkowski

name: David Murray
basis: First went to New York in 1975 and 'lives in New York City'; no other base documented for 1983-91 (Wikipedia).

name: Dexter Gordon
timeline: start: Los Angeles; from 1944: New York; from 1947: Los Angeles; from 1960: New York; from 1963: Copenhagen; from 1976: New York
basis: Back in Los Angeles late 1946 (1947 Dial sessions, duels with Wardell Gray); settled in New York for the 1961-62 Blue Note period; 1962-76 in Europe 'mainly' Paris and Copenhagen (A Day in Copenhagen, 1969) (Wikipedia).

name: Dickie Wells
basis: Member of Count Basie's New York-based band for eleven years, 1938-45 (Wikipedia).

name: Dizzy Gillespie
basis: 52nd Street and Town Hall (June 1945) in New York; Billy Berg's Los Angeles engagement Dec 1945 was a short gig; Manhattan club appearances 1953 (Wikipedia).

name: Don Byas
basis: Went to Europe with Don Redman's band in 1946 and 'remained there, living in France, the Netherlands, and Denmark for the rest of his life' (Britannica).

name: Don Ellis
timeline: start: New York; from 1965: Los Angeles
basis: Moved to Greenwich Village after the army, active in the New York avant-garde scene (George Russell sextet), small-group sessions 1960-62, Improvisational Workshop Orchestra in New York 1963 (Wikipedia).

name: Eric Dolphy
basis: Moved to New York City after leaving Chico Hamilton (1959); Mingus Jazz Workshop and Prestige sessions 1960; Five Spot quintet with Booker Little 1961 (Wikipedia).

name: Fats Navarro
basis: Settled in New York City in 1946; in 1948 with Tadd Dameron's group based at the Royal Roost, New York (Wikipedia).

name: Freddie Hubbard
basis: Moved to New York in 1958; Blue Note debut 1960, Jazz Messengers 1961-64 (Blue Note artist biography).

name: Gerry Mulligan
timeline: start: New York; from 1952: Los Angeles; from 1955: New York
basis: Headed west to Los Angeles in early 1952 (The Haig quartet) until his 1953 arrest; later Concert Jazz Band recorded live at the Village Vanguard, New York; no other base documented for 1957-60 (Wikipedia).

name: Hank Mobley
basis: Introduced to the New York jazz scene in 1951 by Max Roach and composed/recorded there (Blue Note from 1955); no other base documented (Wikipedia).

name: Harry Edison
timeline: start: New York; from 1950: Los Angeles
basis: 'In the early 1950s, he settled on the West Coast' as a Hollywood studio musician (Wikipedia).

name: Henry Allen
basis: Went to New York City to join Luis Russell's band, rejoining in 1937 for three years; 1941 OKeh sessions; no other base documented (Wikipedia).

name: J.C. Higginbotham
basis: Played through the 1940s with Red Allen's New York-based group; no other base documented (Wikipedia).

name: J.J. Johnson
basis: After leaving Basie in 1946 played in small bebop bands in New York clubs; Jay and Kai combo 1954; no other base documented (Wikipedia).

name: Joe Henderson
timeline: start: New York; from 1971: San Francisco
basis: Moved to New York in 1962 on army discharge (Blue Note years 1963-64); 'Henderson moved to San Francisco' in 1971 and lived there for the rest of his life (Wikipedia).

name: Joe Lovano
basis: After three years with Woody Herman 'moved to New York City' to play with the Mel Lewis big band; Blue Note artist from 1990 (Wikipedia).

name: John Coltrane
basis: Left Philadelphia for New York City in 1956; apartment on 103rd St 1957, house in St. Albans, Queens, then Dix Hills, Long Island from 1964 (Wikipedia).

name: Johnny Dodds
basis: Worked regularly at Kelly's Stables, Chicago 1924-30 and recorded the Hot Five/Seven there (Wikipedia).

name: Johnny Hodges
basis: Moved to New York City in 1924; with Duke Ellington's orchestra except 1951-55; died in New York City (Wikipedia).

name: Joshua Redman
basis: After graduating from Harvard in 1991 moved in with friends in Brooklyn and was 'immersed in the New York jazz scene' (Wikipedia).

name: Kai Winding
basis: Raised in New York (Stuyvesant HS 1940) and photographed in New York Jan 1947; no other base documented for 1948 (Wikipedia).

name: Kenny Dorham
basis: Brief undated Los Angeles stay after discharge, otherwise New York: 1963 recording at the Flamboyan, Queens, 1964 Jazz at P.S. 175 (Harlem), died in New York City (Wikipedia).

name: Kenny Garrett
basis: Wikipedia names no base for 1997 (Detroit-born; Songbook on Warner Bros. 1997); New York kept as default.

name: Kenny Wheeler
basis: Moved to London in 1952 and died there in 2014; Banff Centre teaching 1983-98 was a visiting role (Canadian Encyclopedia).

name: Kid Ory
basis: 'In 1925, Ory moved to Chicago' working and recording with Louis Armstrong (Hot Five, Feb 1926) (Wikipedia).

name: Lee Konitz
basis: Working in New York with Tristano/Parker c.1949 ('stuck in New York City' when his child was born); Prestige recordings; no other base documented (Wikipedia).

name: Lee Morgan
basis: 1957 in Dizzy Gillespie's big band and recording for Blue Note; back in Philadelphia 1961-62, then 'on returning to New York in 1963' recorded The Sidewinder (Wikipedia).

name: Lester Young
timeline: start: Kansas City; from 1937: New York
basis: 'Back with Basie in New York City' 1936-40 and guest soloist for New York bands 1941-44 (encyclopedia.com), but he also co-led a band 'in California and New York' with brother Lee (undated), was in Los Angeles when drafted Sept 1944 and was in army custody until discharge Dec 1945 - 1942 and 1945 may be Los Angeles; ours kept.

name: Lionel Hampton
timeline: start: Los Angeles; from 1937: New York
basis: Led his own band at Los Angeles's Paradise Cafe where Goodman discovered him in 1936; then about four years with Goodman's group (Britannica).

name: Louis Armstrong
basis: 'In 1925, Armstrong returned to Chicago'; Hot Five/Seven, Vendome Theatre and Sunset Cafe work 1926-28; returned to New York in 1929 (Wikipedia).

name: Michael Brecker
basis: Moved to New York City in 1969; co-founded Seventh Avenue South club 1977, SNL band early 1980s, died in Manhattan (Wikipedia).

name: Miles Davis
basis: New York-based from 1949; only interruption was St. Louis/Detroit late 1953 to Feb 1954 (about six months) before returning to New York City (Wikipedia).

name: Milt Jackson
basis: Freelanced with leading bop musicians in New York City and died there; no other base documented (Britannica).

name: Nat Adderley
basis: Moved to New York City with his brother after 1955; lived on 112th Street in Harlem in the 1960s (Wikipedia).

name: Pat Martino
basis: Sources do not fix a 1974 base: Philadelphia-born, moved to New York as a teenager (President Hotel on 48th St), returned to Philadelphia after his 1980 surgery (Wikipedia); ours kept.

name: Pat Metheny
basis: Wikipedia: 'He lived in Brazil from the late 1980s to the early 1990s' and now 'lives in New York City' (move date not given), so 1987/1989 are unsettled; ours kept.

name: Paul Desmond
timeline: start: San Francisco; from 1960: New York
basis: Wikipedia: Bay Area work after WWII; living near the Half Note in New York by 1971 and died at his Upper West Side apartment, but no date for the move east, so 1959-64 not settled; ours kept.

name: Pepper Adams
timeline: start: Los Angeles; from 1958: New York
basis: Formed a group in Los Angeles after leaving Kenton (1956-57) and joined Chet Baker April 1957; 'later moved to New York City' (The Cooker late 1957), quintet with Donald Byrd at the Five Spot 1958 (Wikipedia).

name: Phil Woods
basis: Moved to New York in 1948; led his own groups from 1955; with Quincy Jones 1959-61 (Blue Note artist biography).

name: Red Garland
basis: 'Decided to stay in New York' after 1946, working there and in Philadelphia; Miles Davis Quintet 1955-56 (Wikipedia).

name: Rex Stewart
basis: Toured Europe and Australia 1947-51, lived in France (attended Le Cordon Bleu) and appeared in Jacques Becker's French film Rendezvous in July (1950) (Wikipedia).

name: Roy Eldridge
timeline: start: Chicago; from 1939: New York; from 1950: Paris
basis: Moved to Chicago in fall 1936 to form an octet (quit playing in 1938); freelanced in New York 1943, Artie Shaw 1944; moved to Paris in 1950, back to New York 1951 (Wikipedia).

name: Sidney Bechet
basis: Left Noble Sissle in 1938 and 'quickly moved back to New York'; in the early 1940s lived in Brooklyn (encyclopedia.com).

name: Sonny Rollins
basis: Harlem-born, 1954 Miles Davis sessions, Lower East Side/Brooklyn residences, Saxophone Colossus 1956; moved to Germantown NY only in 1972 after Next Album (Wikipedia).

name: Sonny Stitt
basis: Wikipedia names no base for 1946-49 (Bebop Boys 1946, Galaxy 1948, Prestige sessions 1949-50 with Bud Powell and J.J. Johnson); New York kept as default.

name: Stan Getz
basis: Lived in Copenhagen only until 1961, then 'moved back to New York in 1961' (Focus) through Getz/Gilberto 1964; 1957 predates the Copenhagen move (jazz.com).

name: Steve Coleman
basis: Moved to New York in 1978 and built his career there (M-Base); no other base documented for 1988-91 (Wikipedia).

name: Steve Lacy
basis: New York work throughout: Gil Evans 1957, Jazz Gallery 1960, Rudd quartet 1961-64, 'by 1965 Lacy was hardly working in New York' before moving to Europe (jazz.com).

name: Steve Turre
basis: Saturday Night Live band from 1985 and Manhattan School of Music faculty from 1988; resident of Montclair NJ in the New York area (Wikipedia).

name: Von Freeman
basis: 'Returned to Chicago, where he remained for the duration of his career' (Wikipedia).

name: Warne Marsh
timeline: start: New York; from 1966: Los Angeles; from 1976: New York
basis: 1949 recordings with Lennie Tristano (Crosscurrents) and live at Birdland, New York (Wikipedia).

name: Wayne Shorter
basis: Member of Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers (to 1964) and Miles Davis's quintet, both New York-based; Blue Note debut Night Dreamer recorded at Van Gelder's NJ studio 1964; no other base named (Wikipedia).

name: Woody Shaw
basis: 'Returned from California to New York' in 1974 and signed with Columbia in 1977 (New York); Wikipedia also mentions an undated 'lengthy stay in Europe' before returning to the US in early 1989, so 1987 is unsettled - ours kept.

name: Wynton Marsalis
basis: Moved to New York City for Juilliard in fall 1979; artistic director of Classical Jazz at Lincoln Center 1987-90 (official biography).

name: Zoot Sims
basis: Wikipedia's only 1950 location is the recording 'The Zoot Sims Quartet in Paris' (made while touring Europe); no base stated, New York kept.

name: Elvis Presley
basis: Home base Memphis (Sun 1954; Graceland from 1957 to death 1977), with RCA sessions mainly in Nashville and Hollywood (Wikipedia)

name: The Beatles
basis: All records 1962-70 made at EMI/Abbey Road Studios in London, starting with Please Please Me recorded 11 Feb 1963; band moved to London 1963 (Wikipedia)

name: The Rolling Stones
timeline: start: London; from 1971: Los Angeles; from 1974: Munich; from 1977: Paris
basis: London-based 1962-70 (Regent Sound etc.); tax exiles from 1971 (Villa Nellcote, Exile finished at Sunset Sound LA 1972); Musicland Munich 1974-76; Pathe Marconi Paris for Some Girls 1977-78 onward (Wikipedia)

name: The Beach Boys
basis: Formed in Hawthorne (LA County) 1961; recorded in Hollywood studios throughout 1962-89 (Wikipedia)

name: James Brown
basis: Macon-based with Famous Flames 1955-63 recording for King (Cincinnati); house in St. Albans, Queens, New York from mid-1960s (Wikipedia)

name: Brenda Lee
basis: Nashville-based, recorded with Owen Bradley for Decca Nashville from 1958 for ten years (Wikipedia)

name: Chicago
basis: Formed Chicago 1967 but moved to Los Angeles in June 1968 before first album; LA-based thereafter, recording also at Caribou Ranch CO (Wikipedia)

name: Dion
basis: Bronx-based through the 1960s; moved to Boca Raton, Florida only in 1968 (Wikipedia)

name: The Everly Brothers
basis: Nashville-based from 1955 (Cadence); broke with Wesley Rose and moved to California in 1961; Phil stayed in Los Angeles after the 1973 split (Country Music Hall of Fame)
source_title: The Everly Brothers - Country Music Hall of Fame

name: Rolling Stones
timeline: start: London; from 1971: Los Angeles; from 1974: Munich; from 1977: Paris
basis: Duplicate of The Rolling Stones row: London-based 1962-70; tax exiles from 1971 (Exile finished in LA 1972); Musicland Munich 1974-76; Paris sessions from 1977 (Wikipedia)

name: Cyndi Lauper
basis: Queens-born New York singer, discovered in a New York bar 1981; NY-based through the 1980s (Wikipedia)

name: Eric Clapton
basis: Based at his Surrey residence (Hurtwood Edge, near London) throughout 1972-92; recorded abroad on tour (Wikipedia)

name: Kenny Rogers
basis: Los Angeles-based; built Lion Share Studios in LA in 1981 (Wikipedia)

name: Ray Charles
basis: Moved to Los Angeles in 1950 and based there (RPM studio) through the 1960s (Wikipedia)

name: Heart
basis: Members moved to Vancouver c.1972-73 and recorded Dreamboat Annie (1975) at Can-Base/Mushroom Studios there; back in the Seattle scene from the Portrait Records era (1977) (Wikipedia)

name: Stevie Wonder
timeline: start: Detroit; from 1971: New York; from 1974: Los Angeles
basis: Detroit/Motown until 1971; from May 1971 recorded with Margouleff/Cecil in New York; based in Los Angeles after 1973 (Wonderland studio) (Wikipedia)

name: Chuck Berry
basis: Lived in St. Louis (Club Bandstand) while recording for Chess in Chicago 1955-66 and 1970-73 (Wikipedia)

name: John Denver
basis: Lived in Aspen, Colorado from the early 1970s (after Rocky Mountain High, 1972) until his death (Wikipedia)

name: Tina Turner
basis: Private Dancer (1984) recorded 1983-84 at six London studios (Farmyard, Mayfair, Wessex, Good Earth, Abbey Road, CBS); her Capitol-era records were made in England (Wikipedia)

name: Bob Seger
basis: Detroit-area artist with Detroit-area Silver Bullet Band; recorded partly with Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section (Wikipedia)

name: Michael Jackson
basis: Lived at family estate in Encino, Los Angeles from 1971 until buying Neverland in 1988 (Wikipedia)

name: Dr. Hook
basis: A Little Bit More (1976) recorded in Nashville, "now the group's new home base" after signing with Capitol in 1975 (ClassicBands)

name: Elton John

basis: Wikipedia gives Chicago as his hometown and base of his career but does not state where he was based/recording in 1996 (touring that year); kept Chicago
